decisions.reason: As a bread variant very close to the bakery’s existing craft knowledge and shown beyond launch, it fits the firm’s absorptive capacity and can be improved with routine learning from sales and production feedback.

The tour offering disappeared from the website after launch and, while related to the visitor business, it draws more on hospitality than on the firm’s strongest bakery knowledge base, making it a weaker candidate for continued resource use.

This sweet pastry is tightly aligned with the firm’s established confectionery skills and stayed visible after launch, so management would expect to learn from it easily and commercialise it efficiently.

A farmhouse bread sits squarely within the firm’s traditional baking capabilities, so even with limited public evidence it is the kind of incremental product a German bakery can sustain and refine without major new knowledge needs.

The poppy seed Christmas stollen builds directly on core seasonal expertise and its gold award is a strong interpretable signal that the firm can successfully exploit and further improve this product.
The premium Christmas stollen is highly related to the firm’s established recipes and festive range, and the gold award indicates strong market and quality validation worth building on.
